channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero launches with an 88 Metacritic and big early sales
item.description: S-Game's martial arts action game launches October 29 after topping Steam's global sales chart, with sales estimated near 1 million.

item.title: Google Cloud revenue doubles but Alphabet shares fall after hours
item.description: Alphabet's third-quarter revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion as Google Cloud grew 103%, yet shares fell about 9% after hours.

item.title: Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show
item.description: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation said Jay-Z will headline halftime at Super Bowl LXI on February 14 at SoFi Stadium.

item.title: OpenAI is reported to plan buying Google's TPU chips
item.description: OpenAI plans to buy Google's tensor processing units, The Information reports, though neither company has confirmed a deal.

item.title: Microsoft posts a 10th straight record quarter with $92.3 billion revenue
item.description: Microsoft's revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion and net income 32% to $36.6 billion, its tenth record quarter in a row, TechCrunch reports.

item.title: Dune: Part Three gets its final trailer seven weeks before release
item.description: Warner Bros., Legendary and IMAX released the final trailer and poster for Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three, out December 18.

item.title: Pokémon Unite will shut down on March 23, 2027
item.description: The free-to-play Pokémon battle arena game is ending service, and sales of gems and Unite Club memberships stopped on October 27.

item.title: Anthropic says an unreleased model built working exploits for Chrome and Linux
item.description: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says an internal model found flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux and chained them into five exploits.

item.title: Nintendo's Indie World dates Witchbrook and shadow-drops a cleaning game
item.description: Nintendo's 15-minute Indie World gave Witchbrook a January 28, 2027 date and released Bao Bao's Cozy Cleaning Services the same day.

item.title: Anthropic files its S-1 and plans a Nasdaq listing as ANT
item.description: Anthropic's public S-1 sets up a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT and shows revenue growing more than tenfold in a year.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra for fast, cheap computer use
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra is a cheaper, faster OpenAI model built for running software, at half its predecessor's standard API price.

item.title: Anthropic cuts Claude prices 40% for US governments
item.description: An expanded GSA deal gives US federal, state, local and tribal governments 40% off Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the API.

item.title: Susan Saint James, star of McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie, dies at 80
item.description: Emmy-winning actor Susan Saint James died on Monday at 80, Cynopsis reports.

item.title: Xbox promises easier review access after Modern Warfare 4 got two Xbox reviews
item.description: Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet said reviewing games on Xbox takes too many steps, after Modern Warfare 4 drew few Xbox reviews.

item.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a world model with sound and live edits
item.description: Genie 4 generates interactive worlds with native audio, more natural motion and physics, and lets users steer scenes in real time.

item.title: Walter Koenig, Star Trek's original Chekov, dies at 90
item.description: Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov in the original Star Trek series and films, has died at 90.

item.title: About 32.5 million PHP services run versions hit by PHP2Shell flaws
item.description: Censys data shows about 32.5 million internet-exposed PHP services on vulnerable versions, and CISA confirms active exploitation, Cybernews reports.

item.title: Netherlands plans to cut 25,000 government jobs in AI-linked savings
item.description: The Dutch government plans to eliminate about 25,000 state jobs as part of savings tied to AI, Semafor reports.

item.title: Netflix is reported to have cut about 6% of its workforce
item.description: Netflix laid off about 6% of its staff in October, the Los Angeles Times reports, amid a shake-up of its content leadership.

item.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered earns strong reviews before launch
item.description: The remaster of Telltale's Fables adventure averaged 84 on Metacritic ahead of its October 29 release, VGTimes reports.

item.title: Apple adds an AI assistant to Pages, Keynote and Numbers
item.description: Apple's Pages, Keynote and Numbers get an AI assistant that drafts documents, works on slides and analyzes spreadsheet data, The Verge reports.

item.title: Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta's stock offering
item.description: Nvidia is putting $3 billion into Meta's share sale, which Meta priced on October 27 and enlarged to fund AI infrastructure.

item.title: Axiom says AI agents helped computer-verify a 15,000-page math proof
item.description: Axiom says it formally verified the Classification of Finite Simple Groups in the Lean proof language, with AI agents helping over 24 days.

item.title: Jumanji: Open World drops a new trailer ahead of Christmas
item.description: Sony released a new trailer for Jumanji: Open World, which moved to Christmas Day in the US to avoid Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday.

item.title: Brotli decompression flaw triggers patches across Node.js, .NET and Python
item.description: A flaw in Brotli decompression is driving patches across major software platforms, and CISA now lists it as exploited.

item.title: Cloudflare says a cache bug sent some AI replies other customers' data
item.description: A misconfiguration and an SGLang bug let 155 long Workers AI responses include data from other customers' requests, Cloudflare says.

item.title: PS Plus November brings Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Dead Island 2
item.description: Sony's PlayStation Plus monthly games for November are Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered, Dead Island 2 and Monster Train 2, Kotaku reports.

item.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
item.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible staff, more than a quarter of its global workforce.

item.title: Hackers target a critical Oracle E-Business Suite flaw days after its patch
item.description: Attackers are probing an unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite that can lead to remote code execution, The Hacker News reports.

item.title: Minions & Monsters arrives on Peacock
item.description: The animated comedy Minions & Monsters, set in 1927 Hollywood, made its streaming debut on Peacock on October 28.

item.title: Tailscale patches the Tailworm SSH flaws
item.description: Tailscale fixed SSH forwarding flaws that could let an attacker on a trusted device reach root-only services on other servers.

item.title: Keystone will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after its verification key was stolen
item.description: Hardware wallet maker Keystone will destroy unsold devices and rotate its key after an attacker obtained the key used for authenticity checks.

item.title: Anthropic shares early results from six Claude drug-development partnerships
item.description: Anthropic published early results from six drug-development partnerships that use Claude, though most of the work is still preclinical.

item.title: You Can See Everything is tipped to top a quiet Halloween box office
item.description: After rising 25% in its second weekend, the Elizabeth Holmes film is expected to take No. 1 over a quiet Halloween frame.

item.title: SpaceX's $40 billion GPU debt hits neocloud stocks
item.description: SpaceX secured about $40 billion to fund GPUs and data center gear, in what Apollo calls the largest GPU financing ever.

item.title: Xbox offers 25 free games to buyers of eligible Windows 11 PCs
item.description: Buyers of eligible Windows 11 PCs from November 2 through the end of 2026 can claim 25 Xbox games at no extra cost, Pure Xbox reports.

item.title: A 16-year-old UEFI flaw lets attackers run code before Secure Boot
item.description: A long-standing flaw in EDK II firmware lets an attacker on the adjacent network run code during network boot, The Hacker News reports.

item.title: Clayface opens at No. 1 with $24 million in North America
item.description: DC Studios' horror film Clayface won its opening weekend with $24 million in North America.

item.title: Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie star in Peacock comedy Dig, out November 23
item.description: Peacock set a November 23 premiere for Dig, a ten-episode comedy from Amy Poehler and Michael Schur starring Poehler and Hugh Laurie.

item.title: Xbox tells developers to stop identical releases that pad gamerscore
item.description: Xbox is cracking down on near-identical game releases used to inflate achievement scores and will require developers to link versions instead.
